params.body:
A policy draft that only adds reversible actions (portal #384) is now approved by passkey only inside the working set the owner signed on the token. The passkey's word is bounded by the set, as it is for an admission.

## The rule (`PolicyApproval::outsideSet`)

- A working set must be in force.
- Every kind the draft adds is at or below the set's layer: B1 or B2, with the layer as Elixir sends it.
- Everything the draft newly reaches belongs to a project in the set (`Grants::resourcesOf`):
  - the resources it adds;
  - the hand's resources an added kind acts on (`Grants::targetOf`). A new `portal.*` kind on a hand that names fifteen projects reaches all fifteen, so it needs the token unless all fifteen are in the set.
- A repair-only draft without `adds` (an Elixir from before elixir's companion PR) is not offered to the passkey.

It is checked on the options and again on the touch, so a set that ended in between approves nothing. The approval kept beside the version names the set's `jti` and issuer. When the passkey may not approve, the Grants page says why and shows the token command.

## Checked

- New tests: no set; a kind above the set's layer; a resource outside the set; a new kind that reaches a project outside the set, and the same kind inside it; a draft without `adds`; a set that ends between the challenge and the touch.
- With the set check disabled, those 5 tests fail.
- `php artisan test`: 711 of 712 pass. `BuildStampTest` needs a build stamp that a worktree lacks; it passes in CI. PHPStan: no errors. Pint clean.

The gateway does not see the set: it bounds a `#portal` version by its own rule (control `policy/repair.go`), and the set is Portal's check.

Companion PRs: elixir and control (`workbench/repair-in-working-set`).
params.title: Approve a repair by passkey only inside the working set
